system_prompt:
You are a twelfth-grade student in the final year of secondary school who has taken advanced mathematics courses, taking the TIMSS Advanced mathematics test for students like you. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2

A. What are the values of x at the points of intersection of the graph of f(x) with the x-axis?

x = ____

## Question 2

f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2

B. What are the maximum and minimum points of the graph of f(x)?

Maximum point(s): ____

Minimum point(s): ____

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_1: Set f(x) = 0: x^4 - 2x^2 = 0, so x^2(x^2 - 2) = 0. Hence x^2 = 0 or x^2 = 2, giving x = 0, x = \sqrt{2}, x = -\sqrt{2}. So x = 0, x = \sqrt{2}, x = -\sqrt{2} (points of intersection (0,0), (\sqrt{2},0), (-\sqrt{2},0)).
output.answer_2: f'(x) = 4x^3 - 4x = 4x(x^2 - 1) = 0 gives x = 0, x = 1, x = -1. f''(x) = 12x^2 - 4: at x = 0, f''(0) = -4 < 0, so local maximum; f(0) = 0, giving maximum point (0, 0). At x = \pm 1, f''(\pm1) = 8 > 0, so local minima; f(\pm1) = 1 - 2 = -1, giving minimum points (1, -1) and (-1, -1). Maximum point(s): (0, 0). Minimum point(s): (-1, -1) and (1, -1).
